summary: Okanogan County, WA lookout staffed from 1914 to 2020; its 1980 DNR tower was removed in late 2024, and the state planned a camera tower in its place.

facts.design: 14 x 14 ft flat-top live-in cab on a timber tower
facts.agency: Washington State Department of Natural Resources
facts.status_note: Removed in late 2024; no lookout stands on the summit.

access.note: Access to the road has been controversial. TrailChick describes an alternate route over public land that approaches from Sinlahekin Road.

visit.trail_note: TrailChick gives 12.5 miles round trip with about 3,400 feet of gain, by the public-land route from Sinlahekin Road.

events.note: Site first established as a fire camp (TrailChick); a 1914 item calls the Aeneas mountain lookout of the Forest Service

Cab raised 20 feet, per TrailChick; a 1956-58 state report says a lookout was completed in that biennium
DNR timber tower with a 14 x 14 live-in cab; the register gives 40 feet, the other sources 42 feet

corrections.why: The register gives N 48.743015 W 119.622164, and the FFLA list gives 48.74308, -119.62234. The record's point, taken from TrailChick, is about 140 km away from both.

sources.title: Report from the FFLA Washington Chapter for 2024

notes_for_editor: The record's location (47.81203, -120.868, taken from TrailChick) is about 140 km from the register and FFLA positions near Loomis; the correction is proposed, not applied. Other disagreements are written into the story: the tower height (40 ft in the register, 42 ft elsewhere); elevation (5,167 ft in TrailChick, 5,099 ft in the register; the record uses TrailChick); the first year (1914 fire camp in TrailChick and a 1914 item, 1916 for the summer count); and the 1955 observer (Ray Kresek in TrailChick, Willis Erwin in the Gazette-Tribune quote). The FFLA report says the state decided to replace the lookout with a camera tower; no source read confirms that the camera tower was built, so the story does not say so. A Facebook post mentions a wildfire camera on Aeneas, which is not used. The fetch of the Tacoma News Tribune article timed out, so it is not cited.
